category: Physics interfaces V: structural mechanics, MEMS, multibody, rotordynamics & fatigue
description: Structural Mechanics, MEMS, Multibody Dynamics, Rotordynamics, Fatigue and Composite Materials interfaces and features: Membrane, Beam, Truss, Plate, Multibody Dynamics, rotors, Fatigue, Layered Shell; material subnodes (creep, viscoelasticity, damage, thermal expansion, initial stress, damping); connectors, rigid domains, spring foundations, thin elastic layers; constraints and loads (roller, symmetry, prescribed velocity/acceleration, body load, gravity, point/edge loads); the geometric-nonlinearity study setting; and the piezoelectric, electromechanical, thermal-stress, electrostrictive, magnetostrictive and piezoresistive multiphysics interfaces. API: physics().create(tag, type, "geom1"), physics(tag).create(ftag, type, dim), physics(tag).feature("lemm1").create(subtag, type, dim).

tools.name: Membrane (mbrn)
tools.description: Boundary (3D) / edge (2D axisymmetric) structural interface for thin structures with in-plane stiffness only - no bending - such as fabrics, balloons, thin films, biological membranes and prestressed drums. It is intrinsically geometrically nonlinear (a membrane has no stiffness out of plane without tension), supports linear elastic, hyperelastic and layered materials, and can be combined with Shell or Solid for reinforcement layers.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Membrane (mbrn); API: physics().create("mbrn", "Membrane", "geom1")

parameters.name: Thickness d
parameters.description: Membrane thickness on the interface or material node.

parameters.name: Linear Elastic / Hyperelastic Material
parameters.description: Material models; initial stress/prestress subnodes are usually essential for stability.

parameters.name: Face Load / Edge Load / Prescribed Displacement
parameters.description: Loads and constraints on the surface and its edges.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module or MEMS Module. Always include geometric nonlinearity (enabled by default) and give an initial prestress or a stabilising load; a flat unstressed membrane has a singular stiffness matrix.

tools.name: Beam (beam)
tools.description: Edge (3D) / boundary (2D) interface for slender members with axial, bending, shear and torsional stiffness (Euler-Bernoulli or Timoshenko formulations), defined by cross-section data (area, moments of inertia, torsional constant) entered manually or from the built-in common sections (rectangle, box, circular, pipe, H, U, T, C profiles) or from a Beam Cross Section (bcs) 2D analysis. Used for frames, trusses with rigid joints, piping supports, reinforcement in solids and rotor shafts.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Beam (beam); API: physics().create("beam", "HermitianBeam", "geom1")

parameters.name: Cross-Section Data node
parameters.description: SectionType = RectangularSection | BoxSection | CircularSection | PipeSection | H_Profile | U_Profile | T_Profile | C_Profile | HatSection | UserDefined (values in COMSOL 6.4); dimensions such as hy_rect/hz_rect, or A, Izz, Iyy, J for UserDefined.

parameters.name: Section Orientation subnode
parameters.description: Orientation vector or reference point defining the local y axis.

parameters.name: Formulation
parameters.description: Euler-Bernoulli or Timoshenko (shear-flexible).

parameters.name: Point Load / Edge Load / Pinned / Prescribed Displacement/Rotation
parameters.description: Loads and constraints at points and along edges.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. Beam-to-solid and beam-to-shell connections use the Solid-Beam Connection / Shell-Beam Connection multiphysics couplings. Section forces (beam.Nxl, beam.Mzl) and stresses on the section are evaluated with the Beam dataset for 3D visualisation. Section type values verified against the COMSOL 6.4 completion data and example scripts.

tools.name: Truss (truss)
tools.description: Edge interface for members that carry only axial force (no bending): pin-jointed trusses, cables and ropes (with the tension-only/cable option and large deformations), reinforcement bars and springs. Cross-section area is the only section property; geometric nonlinearity turns it into a cable/rope element for sagging conductors and tensile structures.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Truss (truss); API: physics().create("truss", "Truss", "geom1")

parameters.name: Cross-Section Data
parameters.description: Area A.

parameters.name: Linear Elastic Material > Straight Edge Constraint
parameters.description: Keeps elements straight (removes spurious modes) - disable for cables.

parameters.name: Tension only
parameters.description: Option in the material node for cables (no compression).

parameters.name: Pinned / Point Load / Edge Load / Gravity
parameters.description: Constraints and loads.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. Wire (wire) is the dedicated 6.x interface for cables with sag; Pipe Mechanics handles pressurised pipes as beams.

tools.name: Plate (plate)
tools.description: 2D interface for flat thin structures loaded out of plane (Mindlin-Reissner plate theory with optional in-plane membrane DOFs), the 2D analogue of Shell: floor slabs, PCB boards, MEMS plates, diaphragms. Uses displacement w and rotations, supports orthotropic and layered materials, and gives moments/shear forces directly.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Plate (plate) (2D components only); API: physics().create("plate", "Plate", "geom1")

parameters.name: Thickness d
parameters.description: Plate thickness.

parameters.name: Include in-plane displacements
parameters.description: Adds u, v for membrane action.

parameters.name: Face Load / Edge Load / Pinned / Fixed / Simply Supported
parameters.description: Loads and supports.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. For curved or 3D thin structures use Shell; for through-thickness effects in composites use Layered Shell.

tools.name: Multibody Dynamics (mbd)
tools.description: Interface for mechanisms made of rigid and flexible bodies connected by joints (Prismatic, Hinge, Cylindrical, Screw, Planar, Ball, Slot, Reduced Slot, Fixed, Distance, Universal), gears (spur, helical, bevel, worm, rack), cams, springs/dampers and attachments, solving the resulting large-rotation dynamics with contact, friction, joint limits, locking and prescribed motion. Used for engines, robots, landing gear, gear trains, clutches and any mechanism where flexibility of some parts matters; Rigid Domain bodies are cheap, flexible domains use full solid elements.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Multibody Dynamics (mbd); API: physics().create("mbd", "MultibodyDynamics", "geom1")

parameters.name: Rigid Domain / Linear Elastic Material
parameters.description: Choose per domain whether it is rigid (6 DOF) or flexible.

parameters.name: Attachment
parameters.description: Boundary set used as a connection point for joints on flexible bodies.

parameters.name: Joints
parameters.description: Source and destination (attachment or rigid domain), axis, and subnodes: Joint Elasticity, Locking, Constraints (limits), Spring and Damper, Prescribed Motion, Applied Force and Moment, Friction.

parameters.name: Gear Pair / Rack and Pinion / Cam-Follower
parameters.description: Transmission features.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Time Dependent normally; Stationary and Eigenfrequency for equilibrium and modal analysis of the mechanism.

tools.notes: Requires the Multibody Dynamics Module. Joints are global (dimension -1) features referencing bodies. Use Form Assembly when parts must slide; time-dependent runs often need the Generalized alpha solver with tight tolerances for contact.

tools.name: Solid Rotor (rotsld) / Beam Rotor (rotbm)
tools.description: Rotordynamics Module interfaces for rotating shafts with disks and bearings: Solid Rotor models the shaft as a 3D solid in a corotating frame including gyroscopic and centrifugal effects, Beam Rotor uses beam elements for long shafts. Both provide Disk, Bearing (hydrodynamic via Hydrodynamic Bearing interface, journal, thrust, roller, magnetic, foundation), Support, Misalignment and Unbalance features and are solved with Eigenfrequency (Campbell diagrams with the Whirl plot), Frequency Domain (unbalance response) and Time Dependent studies.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Rotordynamics > Solid Rotor (rotsld) or Beam Rotor (rotbm); API: physics().create("rotsld", "SolidRotor", "geom1") / physics().create("rotbm", "BeamRotor", "geom1")

parameters.name: Rotor Axis / Rotational speed Ow
parameters.description: Axis definition and angular speed, typically the parameter of a sweep for Campbell diagrams.

parameters.name: Disk
parameters.description: Rigid disk with mass, inertia and eccentricity (unbalance).

parameters.name: Journal Bearing / Thrust Bearing / Radial Roller Bearing / Foundation
parameters.description: Bearing stiffness/damping (constant, speed dependent, or from Hydrodynamic Bearing physics).

parameters.name: Eigenfrequency study with Campbell plot
parameters.description: Sweep over Ow and plot rotsld.freq with the Whirl and Campbell plots.

tools.notes: Requires the Rotordynamics Module (and Structural Mechanics Module). Hydrodynamic Bearing (hdb) solves the Reynolds equation for oil films and couples through the Solid Rotor Bearing Coupling.

tools.name: Fatigue (ftg)
tools.description: Postprocessing-type interface that evaluates fatigue life or usage factor from the stress/strain history of a structural solution: stress-based (Findley, Matake, Normal stress, Dang Van), strain-based (Smith-Watson-Topper, Wang-Brown, Fatemi-Socie, Morrow), energy-based (Morrow, Darveaux), cumulative damage (Rainflow counting with Palmgren-Miner and S-N curves, Basquin/Coffin-Manson), vibration fatigue from random vibration (PSD), and rubber/ elastomer models. Runs in a dedicated Fatigue study step that references the structural study's load cycle.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Fatigue (ftg); Study > Fatigue; API: physics().create("ftg", "Fatigue", "geom1"); ftg.create("strb1", "StressBased", 3); study.create("ftg", "Fatigue")

parameters.name: Evaluation model node
parameters.description: Stress-Based | Strain-Based | Energy-Based | Cumulative Damage | Harmonic Vibration | Random Vibration; with criterion and material parameters (fatigue limit, S-N data).

parameters.name: Solution to evaluate
parameters.description: Fatigue study step: the study/solution (time steps or load cases) forming one load cycle.

parameters.name: Fatigue model inputs
parameters.description: From the Fatigue material property group of the material.

tools.notes: Requires the Fatigue Module. Results: ftg.fus (fatigue usage factor) or cycles to failure ftg.Nf. The structural study must contain the whole load cycle (a parametric sweep of load cases or a time series).

tools.name: Layered Shell (lshell)
tools.description: Composite Materials Module boundary interface that models laminated shells layer by layer using a layerwise (3D-in-each-layer) theory, so transverse shear, through-thickness stresses, interlaminar delamination (with the Delamination feature), ply-level failure criteria (Tsai-Wu, Hashin, Puck, LaRC03...) and layer-dependent thermal expansion are captured; the lay-up comes from a Layered Material (thickness, angle and material per ply). The Shell interface with a Layered Linear Elastic Material is the cheaper equivalent-single-layer alternative.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Layered Shell (lshell); Global Definitions > Materials > Layered Material; API: physics().create("lshell", "LayeredShell", "geom1")

parameters.name: Layered Material Link / Stack
parameters.description: Assigns the lay-up to the boundary selection.

parameters.name: Linear Elastic Material (layered)
parameters.description: Orthotropic ply properties per layer with fibre angles.

parameters.name: Safety subnode
parameters.description: Composite failure criteria evaluation per layer.

parameters.name: Delamination
parameters.description: Cohesive-zone interface between layers.

parameters.name: Interface/through-thickness plots
parameters.description: Layered Material dataset and Layered Material Slice / Through Thickness plots.

tools.notes: Requires the Composite Materials Module (plus Structural Mechanics Module). Layered materials also feed Heat Transfer in Shells, Electric Currents in Shells and the Piezoelectricity, Layered Shell coupling.

tools.name: Creep
tools.description: Subnode of Linear Elastic Material (and of layered/beam materials) adding time-dependent inelastic strain with Norton, Norton-Bailey, Garofalo (hyperbolic sine), Nabarro-Herring, Coble, Weertman, user-defined or combined primary/secondary/tertiary creep laws, with Arrhenius temperature dependence. Used for high-temperature components (turbine blades, solder joints, polymer parts, concrete) in time-dependent studies; several Creep nodes can be superposed.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Creep (crp1); API: physics("solid").feature("lemm1").create("crp1", "Creep", 3)

parameters.name: Material model
parameters.description: Norton | NortonBailey | Garofalo | NabarroHerring | Coble | Weertman | UserDefined | (Anand for solder in 6.x).

parameters.name: A, n, Q
parameters.description: Creep rate coefficient, stress exponent, activation energy (thermal activation option).

parameters.name: Reference stress / time
parameters.description: Normalisation for the power law.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module (or Geomechanics Module for some laws). Creep strains are internal DOFs (solid.ecr); use a Time Dependent study with strict or adaptive time steps and the Viscoplasticity node for rate-dependent plasticity.

tools.name: Viscoelasticity
tools.description: Subnode of Linear Elastic Material (or Hyperelastic for large strain) adding time/frequency-dependent stiffness via generalized Maxwell, standard linear solid, Kelvin-Voigt, Burgers or fractional-derivative models with any number of branches, optionally with WLF/Arrhenius thermorheological shift and volumetric relaxation. Used for polymers, elastomers, biological tissue and damping layers in time-dependent, frequency-domain (complex modulus) and eigenfrequency (damped modes) studies.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Viscoelasticity (vis1); API: physics("solid").feature("lemm1").create("vis1", "Viscoelasticity", 3)

parameters.name: Material model
parameters.description: GeneralizedMaxwell | StandardLinearSolid | KelvinVoigt | Burgers | GeneralizedKelvinVoigt | FractionalMaxwell...

parameters.name: Branches (Gi, taui)
parameters.description: Shear modulus and relaxation time per branch (Prony series); imported from a table.

parameters.name: Thermal effects
parameters.description: WLF or Arrhenius shift functions with reference temperature.

parameters.name: Static stiffness/Long-term modulus
parameters.description: Choice of how the elastic data is interpreted (instantaneous vs long-term).

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics or MEMS Module (some models need Nonlinear Structural Materials). In the frequency domain the branches give a complex modulus directly; for pure loss-factor damping use the Damping node instead.

tools.name: Damage
tools.description: Subnode of Linear Elastic Material implementing continuum damage for brittle/quasi-brittle materials (concrete, ceramics, composites): scalar damage driven by equivalent strain (Rankine, Mazars, smooth Rankine, Euclidean norm) with exponential or linear/polynomial strain softening and mesh-regularisation by crack-band, implicit gradient or viscous methods; phase-field damage (fracture) is available since 6.0 for crack propagation. Solved incrementally in stationary parametric or time-dependent studies.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Damage (dmg1); API: physics("solid").feature("lemm1").create("dmg1", "Damage", 3)

parameters.name: Damage model
parameters.description: Scalar damage | Phase field damage (6.x) | Mazars damage for concrete.

parameters.name: Equivalent strain / tensile strength / fracture energy
parameters.description: Onset and softening parameters.

parameters.name: Regularization
parameters.description: None | Crack band | Implicit gradient | Viscous.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module or Geomechanics Module. Softening makes the problem ill-conditioned; use displacement control, small load increments and the regularisation length consistent with the mesh.

tools.name: Thermal Expansion (material subnode)
tools.description: Subnode of the structural material nodes (Linear Elastic, Hyperelastic, Plate/Shell/Beam materials) that adds the thermal strain alpha (T - Tref) using the coefficient of thermal expansion (secant or tangent, isotropic or tensor) from the material and a temperature that is either a user expression or a Model Input coupled to a Heat Transfer interface. When a Thermal Expansion multiphysics coupling exists it is created automatically; use the subnode alone for prescribed temperature fields without solving heat transfer.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Thermal Expansion (te1); API: physics("solid").feature("lemm1").create("te1", "ThermalExpansion", 3)

parameters.name: Temperature T
parameters.description: Model input: user defined expression or common model input (linked to ht.T).

parameters.name: Volume reference temperature Tref
parameters.description: Strain-free temperature (default from Default Model Inputs, 293.15 K).

parameters.name: alpha / tangent vs secant CTE
parameters.description: From material; the material library gives temperature-dependent secant values.

tools.notes: Core product feature. Hygroscopic Swelling and Initial Stress and Strain are sibling subnodes for moisture strain and prestress; the coupling version (multiphysics Thermal Expansion, already catalogued) additionally feeds thermoelastic damping back to heat transfer.

tools.name: Initial Stress and Strain
tools.description: Subnode of the structural material nodes that adds an initial (residual) stress tensor and/or an initial strain tensor to the constitutive relation - for prestressed membranes and strings, residual stresses from manufacturing, stresses imported from another study (via withsol) or a lattice-mismatch strain in MEMS/semiconductor films. Prestressed eigenfrequency analyses can use this instead of a preceding stationary step when the stress state is known.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Initial Stress and Strain (iss1); API: physics("solid").feature("lemm1").create("iss1", "InitialStressandStrain", 3)

parameters.name: Sil
parameters.description: Initial stress tensor components (Pa).

parameters.name: eil
parameters.description: Initial strain tensor components.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: For prestress along fibre or local directions.

tools.notes: Core product feature. External Stress is the related subnode for stresses from other physics (e.g. pore pressure, Maxwell stress) that should contribute to equilibrium but not to the strain energy.

tools.name: Rigid Connector
tools.description: Boundary (or edge/point) feature that ties a set of boundaries together as a rigid body with 6 DOF (3 translations, 3 rotations), so loads, constraints, springs, masses and joints can be applied at its centre of rotation; the connected boundaries move rigidly (or, with the flexible option, only in an average sense). It is the way to apply a remote force or moment, model bolts/pins/bearings, connect solids to beams, or attach point masses.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Rigid Connector (rig1); API: physics("solid").create("rig1", "RigidConnector", 2)

parameters.name: Center of rotation
parameters.description: Centroid of selected boundaries, user defined, or a selected point.

parameters.name: Prescribed Displacement/Rotation
parameters.description: Constraints on the connector DOFs (free, constrained, prescribed).

parameters.name: Applied Force / Applied Moment / Mass and Moment of Inertia / Spring Foundation subnodes
parameters.description: Loads and properties at the connector.

parameters.name: Connection type
parameters.description: Rigid | Flexible (average-based, no artificial stiffening).

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module or MEMS Module. Rigid connectors introduce constraint equations coupling many DOFs; the direct solver handles them, and results such as reaction forces are available as solid.rig1.Fx.

tools.name: Rigid Domain
tools.description: Domain material node in Solid Mechanics, Shell and Multibody Dynamics that treats a whole domain as a rigid body with 6 DOF computed from its mass distribution, eliminating internal elastic DOFs. Use it for stiff parts (bolts heads, housings, weights) in assemblies and mechanisms; it still needs a mesh for mass properties and contact, and can carry Applied Force/Moment, Prescribed Displacement/Rotation, Spring Foundation and Mass subnodes.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Material Models > Rigid Domain (rd1); API: physics("solid").create("rd1", "RigidDomain", 3)

parameters.name: Density
parameters.description: From material or user defined for mass and inertia.

parameters.name: Center of rotation
parameters.description: Centre of mass (default) or user defined.

parameters.name: Constraints / loads subnodes
parameters.description: Fixed Constraint, Prescribed Displacement/Rotation, Applied Force, Applied Moment, Spring Foundation, Mass and Moment of Inertia, Location Nodes.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics, MEMS or Multibody Dynamics Module. A rigid domain sharing boundaries with flexible domains is automatically connected; contact between rigid and flexible parts is supported.

tools.name: Spring Foundation
tools.description: Boundary, edge, point or domain feature adding distributed elastic (and viscous) support: a spring stiffness per area/length (total or distributed, linear or from a force-displacement expression) plus optional damping and prestress. Used for elastic supports (Winkler foundation), gaskets, rubber mounts, modelling unmeshed surroundings, and to stabilise underconstrained bodies in stationary studies.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Spring Foundation (spf1); API: physics("solid").create("spf1", "SpringFoundation2", 2)

parameters.name: Spring type
parameters.description: Spring constant per unit area (isotropic/diagonal/symmetric), total spring constant, or force as function of extension.

parameters.name: kPerArea / kTot
parameters.description: Stiffness values.

parameters.name: Loss factor / viscous damping
parameters.description: Damping in frequency and time domain.

parameters.name: Predeformation
parameters.description: Initial extension of the springs.

tools.notes: Core product feature (API type name for the boundary version is SpringFoundation2; SpringFoundation1/0 for edges/points). Thin Elastic Layer is the two-sided version connecting two boundaries with springs; Spring-Damper connects two points/connectors.

tools.name: Thin Elastic Layer
tools.description: Interior boundary or pair feature that connects two sides through a distributed spring (and damper) layer: adhesive layers, gaskets, interface compliance between assembly parts, thermal-interface material mechanics. The layer has zero thickness in the mesh but a stiffness per area (normal and tangential) or a total stiffness; with Form Assembly it works on identity pairs with non-matching meshes.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Thin Elastic Layer (tel1) or Pairs > Thin Elastic Layer; API: physics("solid").create("tel1", "ThinElasticLayer", 2)

parameters.name: kPerArea
parameters.description: Spring constant per unit area (tensor).

parameters.name: Loss factor / viscous damping
parameters.description: Damping properties.

parameters.name: Predeformation
parameters.description: Initial relative displacement.

tools.notes: Core product feature. For a layer with real thickness and material data use Thin Layer (6.x, Solid Mechanics) which computes stiffness from E, nu and thickness.

tools.name: Roller
tools.description: Boundary constraint that fixes the displacement normal to the boundary while leaving tangential motion free (u.n = 0), i.e. a frictionless rigid support or a sliding contact with a rigid plane. Together with Symmetry (identical condition plus symmetry bookkeeping) and Fixed Constraint it covers most supports in stationary structural models.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Roller (roll1); API: physics("solid").create("roll1", "Roller", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries constrained in their normal direction.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Weak constraints for accurate reaction forces; normal direction from boundary or user defined.

tools.notes: Core product feature. On curved boundaries the normal varies, which effectively pins the surface; use a Prescribed Displacement in a local coordinate system if a specific sliding plane is intended.

tools.name: Symmetry (solid mechanics)
tools.description: Boundary condition for symmetry planes of the structure and the load: zero normal displacement (and, in Shell/Plate/Beam, zero in-plane rotations), so half or quarter models can be used. In 6.x the Symmetry node can also apply antisymmetry and a symmetry-plane excitation for periodic cells; Sector Symmetry handles cyclic symmetry with Floquet-type phase for eigenfrequencies of bladed disks.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Symmetry (sym1); API: physics("solid").create("sym1", "SymmetrySolid", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Symmetry planes.

parameters.name: Symmetry type
parameters.description: Symmetry | Antisymmetry (6.x).

parameters.name: Normal direction
parameters.description: From boundary normal or a user-defined axis.

tools.notes: Core product feature. Eigenfrequency analyses on a symmetric half model miss the antisymmetric modes - run both symmetry and antisymmetry cases or use the full model.

tools.name: Prescribed Velocity / Prescribed Acceleration
tools.description: Boundary/edge/point constraints prescribing velocity (frequency-domain and time-dependent studies) or acceleration components instead of displacement, convenient for base excitation of structures (shaker tables, seismic input given as acceleration) and for moving boundaries in transient dynamics. In the frequency domain a prescribed acceleration a0 is equivalent to displacement -a0/omega^2.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > More Constraints > Prescribed Velocity (pv1) / Prescribed Acceleration (pacc1); API: physics("solid").create("pv1", "PrescribedVelocity", 2); create("pacc1", "PrescribedAcceleration", 2)

parameters.name: Prescribed in x/y/z direction
parameters.description: Which components are constrained.

parameters.name: vx/vy/vz or ax/ay/az
parameters.description: Velocity or acceleration expressions.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Local systems for oblique excitations.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module or MEMS Module. For random vibration and response spectrum analyses the base motion is instead specified in the Random Vibration/Response Spectrum study nodes.

tools.name: Body Load
tools.description: Domain load specifying a force per unit volume (or a total force distributed over the selection) - gravity written explicitly (-rho*g), centrifugal/inertial loads, electromagnetic body forces from a Magnetic Fields solution (mf.FLtzx...), or pressure gradients. In 6.x the dedicated Gravity and Rotating Frame nodes are preferred for those specific cases because they also generate mass-consistent terms.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Body Load (bl1); API: physics("solid").create("bl1", "BodyLoad", 3)

parameters.name: Load type
parameters.description: Force per unit volume | Total force | Linear/nonlinear expressions.

parameters.name: FperVol / Ftot
parameters.description: Load vector.

parameters.name: Load group
parameters.description: Assignment to a load group for load-case sweeps.

tools.notes: Core product feature. The Electromagnetic Forces multiphysics coupling adds the Maxwell/Lorentz body load automatically for es/mf + solid problems.

tools.name: Gravity (solid mechanics)
tools.description: Domain feature adding the gravitational body load rho*g in a given direction to selected (or all) structural domains, including rigid domains, point masses and added-mass subnodes, so that self-weight is handled consistently across all structural interfaces in a component. It supports load groups, so gravity can be combined with other load cases.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Gravity (grav1); API: physics("solid").create("grav1", "Gravity", 3)

parameters.name: g
parameters.description: Gravity vector (default {0, 0, -g_const} in 3D).

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains affected (all by default).

tools.notes: Core product feature (5.4+). In a Prestressed Eigenfrequency study gravity enters the stationary step; Rotating Frame is the analogous node for centrifugal/Coriolis loads.

tools.name: Point Load / Edge Load
tools.description: Loads applied at geometry vertices (total force Fp) or along edges (force per unit length or total force), for concentrated forces, line loads, cable pulls and beam/truss loading. In solids a point load produces a singular stress; use it where the local stress is not of interest or apply the load through a Rigid Connector or over a small boundary.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Points > Point Load (pl1) / Edges > Edge Load (el1); API: physics("solid").create("pl1", "PointLoad", 0); create("el1", "EdgeLoad", 1)

parameters.name: Fp
parameters.description: Point force vector (N).

parameters.name: FperLength / Ftot
parameters.description: Edge load per unit length or total force.

parameters.name: Load group
parameters.description: Membership for load cases.

tools.notes: Core product features. Point Load (on Axis) and Ring Load exist for 2D axisymmetric models. Boundary Load (already catalogued) is the area version.

tools.name: Damping (structural)
tools.description: Subnode of the structural material nodes that adds material damping: Rayleigh damping (alpha_dM mass and beta_dK stiffness coefficients, or given as two damping ratios at two frequencies), isotropic loss factor eta_s (frequency domain and eigenfrequency), anisotropic loss factors, viscous damping (bulk/shear viscosity), maximum loss factor and Wave Attenuation models. Needed for realistic frequency-response peaks, damped eigenfrequencies (complex eigenvalues) and energy dissipation in transients.
tools.usage: Physics > Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Damping (dmp1); API: physics("solid").feature("lemm1").create("dmp1", "Damping", 3)

parameters.name: DampingType
parameters.description: RayleighDamping | IsotropicLossFactor | AnisotropicLossFactor | ViscousDamping | MaximumLossFactor | WaveAttenuation.

parameters.name: alpha_dM / beta_dK
parameters.description: Rayleigh coefficients (or f1, zeta1, f2, zeta2 input).

parameters.name: eta_s
parameters.description: Isotropic structural loss factor.

tools.notes: Core product feature. Loss-factor damping is undefined in time-dependent studies (COMSOL warns and ignores it); use Rayleigh or viscoelasticity there. Modal damping ratios can also be set directly in the Frequency Domain, Modal and Time Dependent, Modal study steps.

tools.name: Include Geometric Nonlinearity
tools.description: Study-step setting (Study Settings > Include geometric nonlinearity) that switches structural interfaces from the linear small-strain formulation to a large-deformation (total Lagrangian) formulation with Green-Lagrange strain and second Piola-Kirchhoff stress, and makes follower loads, stress stiffening and large rotations consistent. It is turned on automatically by hyperelastic materials, membranes, contact, moving mesh and prestressed studies, and must be on for buckling post-analysis, snap-through and cable/large-displacement problems.
tools.usage: Study > Stationary/Time Dependent > Study Settings > Include geometric nonlinearity; API: model.study("std1").feature("stat").set("geometricNonlinearity", true)

parameters.name: geometricNonlinearity
parameters.description: true | false on the study step.

parameters.name: Physics-level override
parameters.description: Solid Mechanics > Structural Transient Behavior / Force linear strains option in material nodes to keep linear strains inside a nonlinear frame.

tools.notes: With geometric nonlinearity the spatial frame differs from the material frame: pressure loads follow the deformed surface, and results are evaluated on the deformed configuration unless plotted on the material frame. Linear Buckling uses it implicitly in its second step.

tools.name: Piezoelectricity (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface (Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Piezoelectricity, Solid) that adds Solid Mechanics with a Piezoelectric Material node, Electrostatics with Charge Conservation, Piezoelectric, and the Piezoelectric Effect coupling (pze1); variants exist for Shell, Layered Shell and with the Piezoelectric Waves, Time Explicit interface. Material data (cE/sE, e/d, epsilon_S/T with the IEEE or the 'Voigt' ordering) come from the Piezoelectric material library (PZT, quartz, LiNbO3, PVDF...). Used for transducers, sensors, energy harvesters, SAW/BAW devices and actuators.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Piezoelectricity, Solid; API: physics().create("solid", "SolidMechanics", "geom1"); solid.create("pzm1", "PiezoelectricMaterial", 3); physics().create("es", "Electrostatics", "geom1"); es.create("ccnp1", "ChargeConservationPiezoelectric", 3); multiphysics().create("pze1", "PiezoelectricEffect", 3)

parameters.name: Piezoelectric Material node
parameters.description: Constitutive form (stress-charge or strain-charge), material orientation via a coordinate system for poling direction, damping and dielectric loss subnodes.

parameters.name: Electrodes
parameters.description: Terminal / Ground / Floating Potential on electrode boundaries.

parameters.name: Studies
parameters.description: Stationary, Eigenfrequency (resonance/antiresonance), Frequency Domain (impedance, admittance), Time Dependent.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics, MEMS or Acoustics Module. The poling direction is the local z (3) axis of the material coordinate system; use a Rotated or Cylindrical System for other orientations. The 'Piezoelectric Effect' coupling entry in the earlier chunk covers the coupling node itself.

tools.name: Electromechanics (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined MEMS/Structural interface (Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Electromechanics) combining Solid Mechanics, Electrostatics and the Electromechanical Forces coupling (eme1) plus a Moving Mesh for the air gap, so that electrostatic forces deform the structure and the deformation changes the field: capacitive actuators and switches, comb drives, RF MEMS, electrostatic pull-in analysis, tunable capacitors. Solved with Stationary parametric sweeps of voltage (pull-in), Eigenfrequency (electrostatic spring softening) and Time Dependent studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Electromechanics; API: physics().create("solid", "SolidMechanics", "geom1"); physics().create("es", "Electrostatics", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("eme1", "ElectromechanicalForces", 3); common().create("free1", "FreeDeformation") on the air domains

parameters.name: Electromechanical Forces coupling
parameters.description: Applies the Maxwell stress on the structure boundaries adjacent to the selected (air) domains; option to include Maxwell stress in solid domains (dielectrics).

parameters.name: Moving mesh in the gap
parameters.description: Free Deformation of the air domain, boundaries follow the solid displacement.

parameters.name: Terminal / Ground
parameters.description: Electrode voltages; use a voltage parameter for pull-in sweeps.

tools.notes: Requires the MEMS Module (or AC/DC + Structural Mechanics). Pull-in: sweep the voltage with an auxiliary sweep and let the solver fail at the instability, or use displacement control (Prescribed Displacement with unknown voltage via a Global Equation).

tools.name: Thermal Stress, Solid (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface (Structural Mechanics > Thermal-Structure Interaction > Thermal Stress, Solid) that adds Solid Mechanics, Heat Transfer in Solids and the Thermal Expansion coupling (te1), so temperature fields drive thermal strains and, optionally, thermoelastic damping feeds back into the heat equation. Sibling interfaces: Thermal Stress, Shell / Layered Shell; Joule Heating and Thermal Expansion (adds Electric Currents and Electromagnetic Heating for busbars, fuses and bond wires); Thermoelasticity (fully coupled, for thermoelastic damping in MEMS resonators).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Thermal-Structure Interaction > Thermal Stress, Solid; API: physics().create("solid", "SolidMechanics", "geom1"); physics().create("ht", "HeatTransfer", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("te1", "ThermalExpansion", 3)

parameters.name: Thermal Expansion coupling
parameters.description: Selects the coupled domains; Tref from Default Model Inputs; option for thermoelastic damping.

parameters.name: Study sequence
parameters.description: Usually one Stationary/Time Dependent step solving both; or a two-step one-way study (heat first, then structure) for large models.

tools.notes: Core product (Thermal Stress with Solid Mechanics is available without add-on modules; shell variants need Structural Mechanics Module). For one-way coupling and speed use two study steps with Physics and Variables Selection.

tools.name: Electrostriction / Magnetostriction / Piezoresistivity (MEMS couplings)
tools.description: MEMS Module multiphysics interfaces for smart materials beyond linear piezoelectricity: Electrostriction couples Solid Mechanics and Electrostatics through the quadratic electrostrictive strain (relaxor ferroelectrics, polymers) and the Ferroelectroelasticity variant adds hysteresis/polarization switching; Magnetostriction couples Solid Mechanics with Magnetic Fields through linear (piezomagnetic) or nonlinear (Terfenol-D, Galfenol) magnetostrictive laws for actuators, sensors and transformer noise; Piezoresistivity couples Electric Currents (domain, boundary or shell) with Solid Mechanics through the stress-dependent resistivity tensor for silicon pressure sensors and strain gauges.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Electrostriction / Magnetostriction / Piezoresistivity, Domain Currents; API: multiphysics().create("este1", "ElectrostrictiveEffect", 3) / ("mste1", "Magnetostriction", 3) / ("pzr1", "Piezoresistivity", 3)

parameters.name: Electrostrictive Material / Magnetostrictive Material / Piezoresistive Material nodes
parameters.description: Added in Solid Mechanics or Electric Currents with the coupling coefficients (electrostrictive Q tensor, saturation magnetostriction, piezoresistance pi tensor).

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: solid + es, solid + mf, ec + solid respectively.

parameters.name: Material library
parameters.description: MEMS material library provides silicon piezoresistance coefficients and magnetostrictive alloys.

tools.notes: Requires the MEMS Module (Magnetostriction also with AC/DC + Structural Mechanics). These are nonlinear couplings; use Stationary with parametric continuation of the field/voltage and enable geometric nonlinearity where strains are not small.
